questions.q: A retailer wants churn scores for all 2 million customers once a month, and nobody needs answers in real time. Which option fits best?
options: A real-time endpoint kept running all month
A serverless endpoint called 2 million times
questions.explain: Batch transform runs a job over a dataset in S3, writes results back to S3, and shuts down, which suits large, non-interactive scoring with no persistent endpoint.

questions.q: A batch transform job is given one huge CSV file and five instances. What does the developer guide say happens?
options: All five instances split the file automatically
Only one instance processes the file; the rest are idle
SageMaker converts it to five files
questions.explain: Input S3 objects are mapped to instances by key, so a single file is processed by one instance. Split large data into several files to use more instances.

questions.q: For an input file named input1.csv, what is the batch transform output file called?
questions.explain: The output file has the same name as the input plus the .out extension, with predictions in the same order as the input records.

questions.q: Which settings describe capacity for a serverless endpoint variant instead of an instance type and count?
questions.explain: A serverless variant carries a ServerlessConfig with MemorySizeInMB (1024 to 6144 in 1 GB steps) and MaxConcurrency, with optional ProvisionedConcurrency.

questions.q: Your serverless endpoint's first request after a quiet hour is slow. What is the most likely cause and a remedy?
options: A cold start; provisioned concurrency can keep capacity ready
The model is corrupt; retrain it
questions.explain: Serverless endpoints scale to zero when idle, so the first request pays for launching compute. Provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of workers warm, at extra cost.
